question.:question/problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $P,$ given by

$$
P=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 & 5 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & -4\end{bmatrix}?
$$

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we need to convert $P$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 & 5 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & -4\end{bmatrix} && R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{3} \\  & \sim \begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 & 5 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $P$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns.

question.:question/problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $P,$ given by

$$
P=\begin{bmatrix}-3 & -2 & -5 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{bmatrix}?
$$

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we need to convert $P$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{gathered}P=\begin{bmatrix}-3 & -2 & -5 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{bmatrix} \\ R_{4}:=R_{4}+(-1)R_{3} \\ \sim \begin{bmatrix}-3 & -2 & -5 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}\end{gathered}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $P$ has $4$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $3$rd, $4$th, and $5$th columns.
